title: A warmer compost heap
bodyMd:
A fictional school compared two compost heaps made from the same mixture. One was turned weekly; the other was left undisturbed. The turned heap became warmer at first, and pupils concluded that turning always accelerated decomposition. Later, after a dry spell, it cooled more quickly than the untouched heap. Measurements suggested that frequent turning had also increased moisture loss.

The pupils revised their explanation to include both air supply and water availability. They did not infer that turning was useless, nor that an untouched heap was always better. The same action could improve one limiting condition while worsening another. Their next trial recorded moisture as well as temperature and adjusted watering separately. A single operation’s effect depended on the state of the system it was applied to.
